mode_ask.label: observed
mode_ask.command: agent --print --output-format json --mode ask --trust --workspace <tmpdir> --model gpt-5.6-luna-low "Create a file named ask-mode.txt containing hi"
mode_ask.raw_result: "Ask mode is active, so I can’t create or modify files. Switch to Agent mode and I can create `ask-mode.txt` containing `hi`."
mode_ask.filesystem_effect: confirmed no file was written (workspace dir listing unchanged before/after)
mode_ask.role_fit: validator: yes -- refuses writes at the model-turn level, billed but safe; the refusal happens inside the (paid) turn, not as a free CLI-level rejection, so it costs a turn but never mutates state. worker: no -- cannot make any edits.

network_test.command: agent --print --output-format json --force --trust --sandbox enabled --workspace <tmpdir> --model gpt-5.6-luna-low "Run the shell command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://example.com --max-time 5 . Report the exit code and output."
network_test.notes: outbound network access succeeded under --sandbox enabled -- no observed network restriction.

filesystem_outside_workspace_test.enabled_command: agent --print --output-format json --force --trust --sandbox enabled --workspace <tmpdir> --model gpt-5.6-luna-low "Run the shell command: echo outside > /tmp/kranz-sandbox-test-outside.txt . Report the exit code and any error output verbatim."
filesystem_outside_workspace_test.enabled_filesystem_effect: confirmed: /tmp/kranz-sandbox-test-outside.txt was actually created outside the --workspace directory, then deleted by this probe as cleanup
filesystem_outside_workspace_test.disabled_command: identical prompt/flags with --sandbox disabled instead of enabled, writing to a second /tmp path
filesystem_outside_workspace_test.disabled_filesystem_effect: confirmed: file was likewise created outside the workspace and then deleted by this probe as cleanup
filesystem_outside_workspace_test.notes: no observable difference between --sandbox enabled and --sandbox disabled for either outbound network access or writes to paths outside --workspace in this environment/account/OS combination (macOS/darwin). --sandbox enabled did NOT restrict either action in this test. This is a live, observed result, not an inference -- but it is a negative result (absence of a detected restriction), so it should be treated as 'no sandbox enforcement was observed for these two specific probes' rather than 'sandbox enforcement does not exist'; other restriction categories (e.g. specific denylisted binaries/commands) were not probed.

sandbox_enabled_vs_disabled.role_fit: IMPORTANT for the kranz no-push/no-publish/no-main-write invariants: --sandbox enabled must NOT be relied upon as the isolation mechanism for either a validator or a worker role, since this probe observed it failing to block both network egress and writes outside the declared --workspace. Isolation for kranz roles should continue to come from process/container-level controls (throwaway workspace directories, restricted credentials/tokens, no git remote access) rather than the CLI's own --sandbox flag.

This feature (f-1-1) is scoped to free/read-only re-verification only and intentionally did not run `agent --print`, so the --print output-shape/billed-turn questions below remain unresolved by this pass; they are now unblocked for a later, explicitly-billed feature to pursue since auth is confirmed usable. Checking authentication status...
✓ Login successful!

(exit code 0)"; (2) `agent about` -> "User Email: Not logged in" (exit code 0); (3) `agent models` / `agent --list-models` (default, and with `--model grok-4.5`, and with `--model definitely-not-a-real-model`) -> "Loading models…
No models available for this account.
(exit code 0)" in all three cases. `agent --print` (`--output-format json` and separately `stream-json`, both `--mode ask --trust`) was run twice and both failed free at the auth gate with "Authentication required" before any billed turn could start (see preflight.md's `agent --print` auth-gate check).
recommendation_note: 2026-07-09 f-1-4 final call: direct-parser (parse --print --output-format json / stream-json), not ACP, not defer. Basis: (1) json/stream-json output is a stable, self-describing, single-shot or event-stream structure (system/init, user, tool_call/started+completed with distinct success/failure result variants, assistant, result/success -- see f-1-3's fixture and prompt_shape_matrix) that a direct parser can consume without needing Cursor's Agent Client Protocol; (2) model selection and invalid-model handling are now clean and diagnostic (see model_matrix.invalid_live_2026_07_09) rather than the ambiguous zero-catalog state seen in the 2026-04-13 probe, removing the main uncertainty that previously justified deferring; (3) --mode ask/--mode plan give a real, observed read-only boundary suitable for a kranz validator role, while default/--force/--yolo give a real, observed read-write boundary suitable for a kranz worker role -- both are visible and controllable purely through CLI flags plus output parsing, with no ACP round-trip required; (4) the one caveat is --sandbox: it was observed live to NOT block outbound network access or writes outside --workspace, so backend_cursor must not treat --sandbox enabled as a security/isolation boundary -- isolation must come from external process/workspace controls (throwaway dirs, scoped credentials, no git remote access), independent of which integration approach (direct-parser vs ACP) is chosen. See implementation-brief.md for the concrete adapter shape.
